questions.text: In the checked Metals Lecture, welding joins metals by creating:

options.text: An actual union of interatomic bonds
Only a weak adhesive surface film

questions.rationale: The Metals Lecture defines welding as joining metals so there is an actual union of interatomic bonds.
questions.explanation: GMAW requires external shielding gas supply and is sensitive to wind; better suited for controlled shop environments and production welding. GTAW produces superior weld quality but is slow and requires very high operator skill; used for specialty applications (aluminum, stainless, thin sections), not structural field work. FCAW is suitable for production work and outdoor applications but is less versatile than SMAW for Philippine field conditions. SMAW (Shielded Metal Arc Welding) uses a consumable flux-coated electrode, requires minimal equipment, tolerates windy outdoor conditions, and works in all positions. It is the foundation of TESDA NC II certification and dominates Philippine field structural work.
questions.code_citation: AWS D1.1; TESDA NC II; NSCP 2015 Chapter 5

questions.text: Which pair names the two general types of welding in the checked Metals Lecture?
questions.rationale: The Metals Lecture divides welding into pressure welding and fusion welding.

questions.text: Fusion welding in the checked source is described as welding in which:

options.text: Heat and added metal make the weld

questions.rationale: The Metals Lecture describes fusion welding as using heat and added metal to make the weld.
questions.explanation: Visual Inspection detects only surface defects; it cannot reveal internal voids or lack of fusion. Radiographic Testing (RT) reveals internal defects but requires safety protocols, longer exposure time, and specialized equipment. UT is faster and safer. Magnetic Particle Testing (MT) detects surface and near-surface defects in ferrous materials but does not reveal deep internal voids like UT does. Ultrasonic Testing (UT) uses sound waves to detect internal defects. It is non-destructive, relatively quick, and effective for structural work. UT is increasingly preferred over RT (radiography) due to safety and cost advantages.

questions.text: Which heating methods are source-checked for fusion welding?
questions.rationale: The Metals Lecture lists gas flame and electric arc as heating methods for fusion welding.
questions.explanation: GMAW does not rely on flux coating; the flux is in SMAW electrodes. While GMAW uses external gas, the deposition rate is higher, not lower. GMAW does not use flux coating; this describes SMAW, which has a lower deposition rate. GMAW employs external shielding gas (typically argon-CO₂ mixture) and achieves a higher deposition rate than SMAW, making it economical for production shop welding of high-volume structural members.

questions.text: Why should soldering not be used where a strong joint is required?

options.text: Soldered joints have little tensile, shear, or impact strength
Soldering always makes steel stronger than welding
Soldering is the same as ashlar work

questions.rationale: The Metals Lecture warns that soldered joints have very little tensile, shear, or impact strength.

questions.text: How does the checked Metals Lecture distinguish brazing from ordinary soldering?

options.text: Brazing uses higher operating temperatures and stronger, higher-melting filler alloys
Brazing uses lower temperatures and weaker filler than soldering
Brazing is only Portland cement hydration

questions.rationale: The Metals Lecture describes brazing as higher-temperature soldering using stronger, higher-melting alloys.

questions.text: When is brazing generally used according to the checked source?

options.text: Where shape, position, or metal composition is not adaptable to welding
Only when concrete water-cement ratio is too low

questions.rationale: The Metals Lecture states brazing is generally used where shape, position, or composition is not adaptable to welding.

questions.text: According to BCI, steel beam connections may use:

options.text: Various connectors and combinations of bolts and welds

questions.rationale: BCI states steel connections can use different connectors and combinations of bolts and welds.

questions.text: What does BCI say connection strength depends on?

options.text: Member sizes, connecting tees/angles/plates, and bolt or weld configuration
Only the color of aluminum finish
Only the moisture content of cement paste

questions.rationale: BCI ties connection strength to member sizes, connecting plates or angles, and bolt or weld configuration.
questions.explanation: Philippine standards allow non-prequalified joints if properly qualified; they are not prohibited. Prequalified joints meet a defined standard; non-prequalified joints may be equally strong if properly qualified, but qualification is expensive. Material cost is not affected; the concern is qualification testing cost and schedule impact. Prequalified joints have been extensively tested and are approved by AWS D1.1 without requiring individual qualification. Non-prequalified joints must undergo custom testing (tension, bend, CVN impact tests) to demonstrate compliance—a costly process that delays fabrication. For cost and schedule efficiency, designers should default to prequalified joints unless there is a compelling reason otherwise.
